title: List-decoding over a q-ary alphabet
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite field, write $q = \abs{\alpha}$ for the number of its elements, and fix a real number $p$ with $0 < p \le 1 - \tfrac{1}{q}$ together with an integer $L \ge 1$. In this regime one considers block codes over the alphabet $\alpha$ that admit list decoding from a $p$-fraction of symbol errors with output lists of size at most $L$, and the associated rate $r$ they can achieve.
hypotheses_covered: α is a finite (nonempty, decidable) field
q equals the cardinality of α
L is a natural number with 1 ≤ L
caveat: The formal statement carries only hypotheses (a finite field α with q = |α|, a rate parameter p ∈ (0, 1 − 1/q], and a list size L ≥ 1); its conclusion is a bare placeholder (`let r := sorry`) that asserts no proposition. No claim can therefore be faithfully rendered, only the setting. The `current` text (existence of rate-$(1 - H_q(p) - 1/L)$ codes that are $(p,L)$-list-decodable) is the presumed intent but is absent from the Lean, so it is not stated here.
replaced:
For any $q=|\alpha|$, $0<\rho\le 1-1/q$, and $L\ge 1$, there exist codes of rate
$r = 1-H_q(\rho)-1/L$ that are $(\rho,L)$-list-decodable.
